questions.question: Economic activities that involve exploiting natural resources directly (such as agriculture, dairy, fishing, and forestry) belong to the:
options: Primary Sector
Secondary Sector
Tertiary Sector
Quaternary Sector
questions.explanation: When we produce a good by exploiting natural resources, it is an activity of the primary sector. This is because it forms the base for all other products that we subsequently make.

questions.question: The sector that covers activities in which natural products are changed into other forms through manufacturing processes associated with industrial activity is the:
options: Secondary Sector (Industrial Sector)
Primary Sector
Tertiary Sector
Agrarian Sector
questions.explanation: The secondary sector covers activities in which natural products are changed into other forms through ways of manufacturing that we associate with industrial activity. For example, using sugarcane as a raw material to make sugar or gur.

questions.question: Activities that help in the development of the primary and secondary sectors by providing transport, storage, communication, and banking are classified under the:
options: Tertiary Sector (Service Sector)
Primary Sector
Secondary Sector
Extractive Sector
questions.explanation: These are activities that help in the development of the primary and secondary sectors. These activities, by themselves, do not produce a good but they are an aid or a support for the production process. Since these activities generate services, the tertiary sector is also called the service sector.

questions.question: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of a country is defined as:
options: The value of all final goods and services produced within a country during a particular year
The total market value of all intermediate raw materials traded in agricultural mandis
The total gold reserves stored in the vaults of the central bank
The annual value of all foreign remittances sent by overseas citizens
questions.explanation: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is the value of all final goods and services produced within a country during a particular year. It shows how big the economy is.

questions.question: Why are only 'final goods and services' counted when calculating Gross Domestic Product?
options: Because the value of final goods already includes the value of all intermediate goods used in making the final product
Because intermediate goods have zero monetary value in wholesale markets
Because government tax inspectors refuse to inspect raw material receipts
Because intermediate goods are only produced by foreign multinational companies
questions.explanation: The value of final goods already includes the value of all the intermediate goods that are used in making the final good. For instance, the value of biscuits (final good) already includes the value of flour, sugar, and oil (intermediate goods). Counting intermediate goods separately would lead to double counting.

questions.question: In the historical trajectory of today's developed nations, what was the typical sequence of sectoral dominance over time?
options: Primary sector dominant first -> Secondary (manufacturing) sector dominant -> Tertiary (service) sector dominant
Tertiary sector dominant first -> Primary sector -> Secondary sector
Secondary sector dominant first -> Primary sector -> Tertiary sector
All three sectors remained at exactly 33.3% share throughout history
questions.explanation: Historically, primary sector was the most important sector in the initial stages of development. With new manufacturing methods, factories came up and the secondary sector became dominant. In the past 100 years, there has been a further shift from secondary to tertiary sector in developed countries.

questions.subtopic: Rising Importance of Tertiary Sector in India
questions.question: Which of the following is a primary reason for the rapid growth of the tertiary sector in India over the past few decades?
options: The government's responsibility to provide basic services like hospitals, schools, police stations, transport, and banking
A complete shutdown of all agricultural farming and livestock rearing
The legal prohibition of manufacturing factories in urban centres
The elimination of personal computers and internet services
questions.explanation: In any country several basic services such as hospitals, educational institutions, post and telegraph services, police stations, courts, defense, transport, banks, and insurance are required. In a developing country, the government has to take responsibility for the provision of these services.

questions.subtopic: Employment vs GDP Mismatch in India
questions.question: While the tertiary sector contributes the largest share to India's GDP (over 50%), where does the largest proportion of the Indian workforce still remain employed?
options: In the Primary (Agricultural) Sector
In the Heavy Industrial Manufacturing Sector
In the Information Technology and BPO Sector
In the Commercial Banking and Insurance Sector
questions.explanation: A remarkable fact about India is that while there has been a change in the share of the three sectors in GDP, a similar shift has not taken place in employment. The primary sector continues to be the largest employer in India (employing over 44% of workers).

questions.question: What is 'disguised unemployment' (or underemployment) which is prevalent in Indian agriculture?
options: A situation where more people work on a farm than necessary, such that removing some workers does not reduce total crop production
Workers who disguise their identity to avoid paying income taxes
Workers who are unemployed during off-monsoon winter months
Factory employees who work night shifts in textile mills
questions.explanation: Underemployment or disguised unemployment occurs when people are apparently working but all of them are made to work less than their potential. Even if you move a few people out, production will not be affected because they are surplus labour.

questions.question: In the NCERT textbook example, farmer Laxmi owns a two-hectare unirrigated plot and all five family members work on it throughout the year. Why is this considered disguised unemployment?
options: Each member does some work but none is fully employed; if two members take up outside wage labour, total farm output remains unchanged
Laxmi's family produces crops exclusively for export to European markets
The plot is owned by a multinational corporate conglomerate
The family members receive salaries directly from the state treasury
questions.explanation: All five members work on the small plot because they have nowhere else to go for work. Each one does some work, but no one is fully employed. If two members move out to work in a mill, the family earns extra cash income while agricultural harvest remains the same.

questions.subtopic: Creating Rural Employment: Irrigation and Infrastructure
questions.question: How can the government directly reduce agricultural underemployment and create rural jobs?
options: By constructing irrigation canals, check dams, and rural roads to connect villages with markets and enable multi-cropping
By banning farmers from using tractors and organic seeds
By evicting small farmers from their ancestral village lands
By forcing all villagers to purchase commercial airline tickets
questions.explanation: If government spends some money on constructing a well or canals, farmers can irrigate their land and take a second crop (like wheat or pulses). This creates employment on the farm itself. Building rural roads and cold storages creates transport and marketing jobs.

questions.question: What is the primary statutory guarantee provided under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA 2005)?
options: 100 days of guaranteed wage employment in a year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work
Free tractors and diesel fuel to all agricultural landholders
365 days of salaried employment in urban corporate software firms
Full monthly pensions to all citizens over the age of twenty-one
questions.explanation: Under MGNREGA 2005, all those who are able to, and are in need of, work in rural areas are guaranteed 100 days of employment in a year by the government.

questions.question: Under MGNREGA 2005, what happens if the government fails to provide employment within 15 days of an application?
options: The government is legally obligated to pay a daily unemployment allowance to the applicant
The applicant must forfeit their voter registration card
The village sarpanch is immediately dismissed by the Supreme Court
The applicant is allotted two hectares of central government forest land
questions.explanation: If the government fails in its duty to provide employment within 15 days, it gives unemployment allowances to the people. This is why it is known as the 'Right to Work'.

questions.question: Which of the following is a hallmark characteristic of employment in the 'Organised Sector'?
options: Jobs have formal appointment letters, security of employment, fixed working hours, and benefits like paid leave and provident fund
Wages are paid randomly in cash with no formal payroll records
Workers can be arbitrarily fired on any morning without notice or cause
Workplaces are completely outside the scope of labour laws and Factory Acts
questions.explanation: Organised sector covers those enterprises where the terms of employment are regular and people have assured work. They are registered by government and have to follow rules like the Factories Act, Minimum Wages Act, Payment of Gratuity Act, providing job security and statutory benefits.

questions.question: What is the primary condition of work in the 'Unorganised Sector' in India?
options: Jobs are low-paid, often irregular, lack job security, and offer no provision for overtime pay, paid holidays, or medical leave
Workers receive double pay for every hour of overtime worked
Employees are covered by comprehensive group health insurance schemes
Workers are represented by constitutionally recognized collective bargaining unions
questions.explanation: The unorganised sector is characterised by small and scattered units which are largely outside the control of the government. Jobs here are low-paid and often not regular. There is no provision for overtime, paid leave, holidays, leave due to sickness, etc.

questions.question: In the NCERT case study comparing Kanta (office worker) and Kamal (grocery store assistant), why is Kamal considered to be in the unorganised sector?
options: Kamal works from 7:30 AM to 8:00 PM without overtime pay, gets no paid leave, has no formal appointment letter, and can be told to leave at any time
Kamal receives a monthly provident fund statement from the central government
Kamal gets free medical treatment at an executive corporate hospital
Kamal works only two hours on weekends
questions.explanation: Kamal works in a small grocery store without formal appointment, works long hours without overtime pay, receives no paid holidays, and has no job security. Hence, he is in the unorganised sector.

questions.question: In rural areas, who constitutes the bulk of vulnerable workers needing state protection in the unorganised sector?
options: Landless agricultural labourers, small and marginal farmers, sharecroppers, and traditional artisans (weavers, blacksmiths, carpenters)
Senior bank executives and financial fund managers
Software architects working in metropolitan cyber parks
Supreme Court senior advocates and corporate attorneys
questions.explanation: In rural areas, the unorganised sector mostly comprises landless agricultural labourers, small and marginal farmers, sharecroppers and artisans (such as weavers, blacksmiths, carpenters and goldsmiths).

questions.question: Economic activities are classified into 'Public Sector' and 'Private Sector' on the basis of:
options: Ownership of assets and delivery of services (government vs private individuals/companies)
The physical weight of the finished manufactured goods
The geographical distance of factories from international seaports
The number of female employees in administrative management
questions.explanation: Another way of classifying economic activities is based on who owns assets and is responsible for the delivery of services: in the public sector, the government owns most assets and provides services; in the private sector, ownership of assets is in the hands of private individuals or companies.

questions.question: What is the primary driving motivation behind economic activities undertaken by the Public Sector (such as Indian Railways and Post Office)?
options: Social welfare and public benefit at affordable, subsidized rates
Maximizing quarterly corporate profits for private equity shareholders
Eliminating all competition to create private business monopolies
Transferring state revenues to offshore foreign bank accounts
questions.explanation: Activities in the private sector are guided by the motive to earn profits. The purpose of the public sector is not just to earn profits. Governments raise money through taxes and other ways to meet expenses on the services rendered by it for public welfare.

questions.subtopic: Why Government Must Invest in Heavy Infrastructure
questions.question: Why cannot the private sector alone be expected to build mega infrastructure like railways, multipurpose dams, and ports?
options: These projects require astronomical capital investments with very long gestation periods and cannot easily collect profits from millions of individual users
The private sector is legally barred by the constitution from operating heavy machinery
Engineers refuse to work for private commercial enterprises
Infrastructure construction has zero impact on national economic development
questions.explanation: There are several things needed by society as a whole which the private sector will not provide at reasonable cost. These require huge spending which is beyond the capacity of the private sector, and collecting money from thousands of users is difficult. Thus, governments have to undertake heavy spending.
